pages.title: OpenWiki — SSSS
pages.purpose: Root index for this SSSS repo's OpenWiki. Distinguishes the two layers present in the repo — the SSSS reference implementation (spec/registry/kernel/bundle/runtime/semantic) and the Total Recall brain/IDE operational layer — and routes into the concept/workflow/operations/integrations pages.
instructions: Do not put secrets here; note that credentials go through the Total Recall auth plugin (see integrations page).
Regenerate the existing generic brain-boilerplate README into a repo-specific index for the SSSS codebase.

pages.title: SSSS system architecture
pages.purpose: System architecture overview: the layers of the dependency-free reference implementation (spec → registry/schemas → frontmatter → validator → kernel → adapters → runtime/semantic/bundle → CLI/transports), how data flows from a Markdown vault through the Operation Contract to an immutable event log, and the vault→bundle→tenant lifecycle. Includes a Mermaid diagram of the layered architecture and the commit/lifecycle flow.
instructions: Call out that the engine.mjs is a thin façade over kernel.mjs and that the kernel owns all mutation semantics.
Regenerate the existing generic 'this brain' placeholder into the real SSSS system architecture.
Use the mermaid-diagrams skill to render the layered architecture and the vault→bundle→tenant lifecycle diagram.

pages.title: Bundle format & provisioning contract
pages.purpose: The .ucw bundle format (spec §16) and provisioning contract (spec §17): manifest/files/provenance shape, content-hash integrity, parameters and provisioning steps/binding vocabulary, the three pure-ish verbs (export/provision/import), determinism (frozen timestamp, path-sorted canonical serialization), idempotency keys (sha256(workspace:path)), id-remap/prefix, link integrity, and upgrade via structural patches.
instructions: Cover the PROFILE_INCLUDES filter (backup/template/sale) and the portability-driven requirement declaration generation for resource_bound primitives.
Explain that import preflights every envelope before the first commit so a late schema/reference/authorization failure cannot leave a partial import, and that re-import commits zero (idempotent).
Reference upgradeBundle structural patches (§17.4).

pages.title: Operation Contract & mutation kernel
pages.purpose: The spec §6 Operation Contract: the four envelope types (operation/patch/event/delete), the kernel.execute stages (auth → idempotency replay → validation → lease → VFS compare-and-swap commit → event append → intent journal → projection), idempotency replay vs. conflict, the symbolic ERROR_CODES and how transports map them to HTTP status, and the index.md special case.
instructions: Cover fail-closed authorization: missing actor.role is denied, system/admin bypass semantics, event envelopes gated on write:event.

Explain the 0.9 capability authorization model (verified principal, requiredCapabilities, capabilityCovers with path glob @ scoping, policyFloors) and the legacy role→capability translation in engine.mjs.
Reference symbolic failure codes and ERROR_STATUS mapping.

pages.title: Registry, portability & schemas
pages.purpose: Registry-driven type resolution and the portability keystone: core.json document/contract primitives, extension registry composition, aliases, required/optional/immutable/required_when/patterns/references/enums/resource fields, the three portability classes (structural/tenant_private/resource_bound) and export profiles (backup/template/sale), the zero-dependency YAML frontmatter parser, the Draft 2020-12 JSON Schemas and the zero-dependency schema-validator.
instructions: Cover x_portability override (most restrictive wins) and how resource_bound fields become REQUIREMENT placeholders in template/sale exports.
Explain that the engine has no per-type code: required_fields, append_only, portability, and reference constraints all come from the registry.
Note validateData/validateDocument/createValidator in validator.mjs and the primitive-definition API in primitive.mjs.

pages.title: Host adapter contracts
pages.purpose: The host-injectable adapter contracts and their file-based reference implementations: VFS (MemoryVfs/FileSystemVfs, preconditions, VFS_LOCK_DIR/VFS_INTENT_DIR reserved dirs), event store (JsonlEventStore rotation/cursor replay, idempotentEventId), lease store, idempotency store (retention/pruning), intent journal, projection coordinator (sql/search adapters, cursor-aware replay), the guard, UI projection registry, and cross-process file-lock concurrency semantics.
instructions: Cover durable-fs fsyncDirectory/writeFileSyncDurable and the symlinked-lock refusal.
Document the concurrency guarantees table (event append, VFS write/remove, lease acquire/renew/release, idempotency put) with their lock files and stale/timeout behavior.
Note that hosts own durable destination writes for projections; the reference adapters only prove the apply/reset/snapshot contract.

pages.title: Total Recall brain, IDE & secrets
pages.purpose: The operational/brain layer of this repo: it is operated as a Total Recall brain. Covers IDE personalization connectors (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursor/rules/GEMINI.md managed inject markers), the Total Recall memory CLI (remember/recall/compile/context), secrets handled exclusively through the auth plugin (never in OpenWiki or IDE instruction files), the skills system (.agent/skills and /skills SKILL.md libraries, SSSS-related skills like rbac-fail-open-auditor and ssss-registry-parity-auditor), and how AGENTS.md documents the installed plugin namespace surface.
instructions: Consolidate the four existing thin brain pages (ide.md, memory.md, secrets.md, skills.md) into this single integrations page; those pages are being deleted in this plan.
Cover the SSSS-specific agent skills that audit this repo's own invariants (rbac-fail-open-auditor, ssss-registry-parity-auditor, ssss, ssss-project-management) and where their SKILL.md files live.

Emphasize the hard rule: never put API keys or secrets in OpenWiki pages or compiled IDE instruction files — credentials go through the Total Recall auth plugin (auth secret set/get/rotate) following TR_SECRETS_BRAIN.

pages.title: CLI & transports
pages.purpose: The `ssss` CLI dispatcher (scripts/ssss.mjs → cmd-*.mjs modules), the reference HTTP server (cmd-serve.mjs + http.mjs: POST /v1/operations, bearer token, /health), the stdin/stdout JSON bridge (cmd-bridge.mjs for non-JS hosts), and the authoring/schema commands: primitive, registry, schema, migrate, adapter conformance. Includes the scripts/lib/cli.mjs arg parsing and the package exports map.
instructions: Cover the serve/bridge shared engine construction and that HTTP is a façade over kernel.execute, never a writer.

Document the package `exports` subpaths (kernel, engine, runtime, bundle, semantic, vfs, identity, leases, idempotency, intents, events, projections, ui, http, guard, schema-validator, schemas/*) since these are the public library surface.

pages.title: Conformance & test suites
pages.purpose: How the repo proves correctness: `ssss conformance` (structural) / `--engine` (replay fixtures + reference bundle round-trip + workflow runtime checks) / `--endpoint` (diff against a live host), the npm test composite (conformance --engine + check-events-streaming + check-frontmatter + check-commit-durability), conformance-09.mjs kernel suites, the guard.mjs direct-write detector, and the audit/validate-skills helper scripts.
instructions: Cover the durability tests that kill real child processes (not simulated) to prove a committed key is never executed twice and the vault/event log agree after a crash.
Cover the reference bundle round-trip assertions (no tenant_private on disk, second import commits zero).
Note the guard.mjs WRITE_PATTERNS and the `ssss-direct-write-approved` escape hatch.

pages.title: Mutation & commit workflow
pages.purpose: End-to-end control/data flow for a single Operation Contract request through the kernel: envelope validation → verified-principal auth → idempotency replay (store + event log) → expected_before_hash optimistic concurrency → registry validation + reference resolution → lease check → intent journal → VFS compare-and-swap write → event append → idempotency record → projection apply, plus crashed-holder intent recovery and the dry-run/no-op paths. Render as a Mermaid sequence/flowchart.
instructions: Cover the recovery-once behavior and FileIntentJournal vs. MemoryIntentJournal, plus INTENT_OUTCOMES.
Cover the two-winner concurrency resolution: VFS CAS for operation/patch/delete vs. idempotentEventId (UUIDv5) for event envelopes, and the loser re-read/replay path.
Use the mermaid-diagrams skill to render the kernel commit sequence and the intent-recovery decision flow.

pages.title: Semantic projection & search
pages.purpose: The §11.9 semantic system: buildSemanticIndex walks validated Markdown, extracts lexical tokens (NFKC, Unicode-aware), graph edges (relations, [[wiki]] links, Markdown links), deterministic weighted ranking, privacy filters (only structural indexed by default; --include-private requires authorization), multilingual normalizeLanguage, injected embedding adapters, runtime rendering with symbolic controls fixed, and the CLI `ssss semantic`.
instructions: Cover the privacy/output-safety invariants: symlinked vault entries and unsafe paths fail closed, --out must be a regular file outside the source vault with atomic writes.
Note that the projection is disposable — the vault is the only source of truth — and that presentation may change language but never symbolic controls or authorization.

pages.title: Vault → bundle → tenant lifecycle
pages.purpose: The export → validate → inspect → provision → import → upgrade lifecycle as a runnable workflow, including the `ssss new` scaffold (starter vault, dependency-free conformance test, optional --with-total-recall), how params/links are resolved, and the in-one-step import path. Render the lifecycle as a Mermaid diagram.
instructions: Cover the scaffolded project layout and that `ssss new` shells out via execFileSync (no shell, no interpolation) to avoid command injection.
Explain the import summary counts (committed / unchanged-idempotent / failed) and --dry-run.
Use the mermaid-diagrams skill to render the vault→bundle→provision→import→upgrade lifecycle.

pages.title: Workflow runtime planning
pages.purpose: The §11.8 workflow runtime: workflows define triggers in frontmatter (manual/cron/interval/event/webhook/file_change/condition), runtime.mjs is a deterministic planning layer (not a daemon) that turns a trigger into event/task/run Operation Contract envelopes, the canonical loop (workflow_triggered → task → lease/claim → run → task patch → projection), idempotency basis (workspace_id+workflow_id+trigger_id+scheduled_for), and run statuses.
instructions: Cover planWorkflowTrigger, createRunEnvelope, subjectMatches/triggerMatchesEvent glob semantics, and misfire/concurrency policies.
Emphasize that a daemon MUST NOT write vault files directly — every mutation goes through the Operation Contract.
Use the mermaid-diagrams skill to render the workflow trigger→envelopes planning loop.

pages.title: Quickstart — SSSS repo
pages.purpose: Init page that routes a coding agent through the OpenWiki hierarchy for this SSSS reference implementation: which page to read first for the spec/kernel, bundle lifecycle, workflow runtime, semantic index, CLI/transports, conformance, and the Total Recall brain layer. Includes the one-command entrypoints (`ssss new`, `ssss conformance --engine`, `npm test`, `ssss serve`/`bridge`) and a task→page routing map.
instructions: Keep it concise and link-heavy, not a re-explanation of systems.
Map common agent tasks (add a primitive, change the kernel, fix a bundle bug, add a CLI command, run tests, wire a host adapter, manage memory/secrets) to the right OpenWiki page.
This page is required for every plan and must route readers through the hierarchy; generated index pages provide folder navigation and must not be duplicated here.
